subject: MAP: unit-econ check & eval timeline — CardiaHealth
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Cardia MAP — draft checklist for unit-econ gating

Team — drafting the MAP section that answers the finance/procurement checks for CardiaHealth. They asked for a concise unit-econ summary tied to the eval plan and a clear close timeline (pilot -> purchase order). Can you review the bullets below and add gaps/asks? I want to send this to Kelsey by EOD Monday PDT.

Draft bullets (short):
- Purpose: confirm tokens/$ assumptions for pilot and full production, surface caching & batching levers, and align on acceptance gating for MAP close.
- Cost model inputs we will request from them: expected daily requests, avg tokens per request (prompt + response), target latency (P95), and percent of conversational vs. single-turn traffic.
- Redwood outputs: tokens-per-dollar sensitivity for 3 model variants (base open-7b, optimized-7b-quant, safety-fallback-3b), expected per-request cost ranges for pilot (1k qps/day) and scale (50k qps/day), estimated LUT for caching hit-rate impact (0%, 20%, 50%).
- Evaluation plan tie-ins: sample prompt set (500 pairs) + perf runs (3 sequence lengths) to validate token counts and latency under a 95th percentile window; run with/without prefix caching to measure delta.
- Acceptance gates: unit-econ within X% of forecast (TBD), P95 latency <= 400ms on the dedicated pool for critical routes, no more than 2 regressions in quality metrics across eval set.
- Timeline (proposed): discovery + traffic handoff (week 0), eval run (week 1), cost reconciliation & pilot SOW (week 2), pilot onboarding (week 3).

Specific asks for Rishi/Neha:
- Rishi: please draft the tokens/$ sensitivity table (3 variants) and a short paragraph describing batching/caching trade-offs we should send.
- Neha: list the minimal telemetry/metrics Cardia needs to capture during pilot (tokens, cache hit-rate, tail latency, error rate) and an ops checklist for MAP handoff.

I'll compile and send to Kelsey for their inputs.

Thanks,
Olga

Nice start — added a few pragmatic numbers inline below for Olga to consider before we send:

- Tokens/$ (baseline assumptions): open-7b base = 0.00018 $/token (baseline hosted); optimized-7b-quant = 0.00009 $/token; safety-fallback-3b = 0.000035 $/token. These are ballpark; final numbers depend on batching & KV cache savings.
- Batching assumptions: typical batching window 10–25ms for steady traffic; effective tokens-per-batch reduces per-token kernel launch overhead by ~10–25% depending on sequence length. For MAP, show 3 scenarios: no batching (low-load), modest batching (steady), aggressive batching (high concurrency).
- Caching assumptions: prefix cache hit converts full request to near-zero generation cost for repeated prompts; assume 0%, 20%, 40% hit scenarios with linear cost reductions (not perfect but conservative).

I'll attach a quick sensitivity table and short blurb. Neha — can you add the telemetry list?

-Rishi

Adding the telemetry + ops items:

Telemetry (minimum during pilot):
- Total tokens in/out per route (5s granularity)
- Cache hit-rate by route (prefix and KV separate)
- Average and P95 latency (generation + end-to-end)
- Tokens per request distribution (p50/p90/p99)
- Error rate and throttled requests
- Model variant used per request (for fallback accounting)

Ops handoff checklist (MAP):
1) Traffic sample CSV (at least 14 days, anonymized) — requester: Cardia
2) SLOs & route priority doc — requester: Cardia + Solutions
3) Eval prompt set (500) + acceptance criteria — Redwood to provide
4) Billing expectations + forecast spreadsheet (we will provide template)
5) Access for Cardia to pilot telemetry dashboard + runbook

I'll add the above to the spreadsheet Olga mentioned.

-Neha

Thanks Olga — this looks helpful. A few clarifying requests from our side before you finalize the MAP: 

1) Can you provide a one-page unit-econ summary (tokens/$) for the three model variants you listed? We need a short table we can circulate to procurement and finance.
2) For caching: can you explain how prefix caching vs. KV caching impacts the pilot acceptance criteria? We expect a significant fraction of repeated prompts in clinician flows.
3) Pilot traffic: we can provide a 7-day anonymized sample CSV tomorrow — will that be enough?
4) Timeline: procurement prefers a clear PO milestone — can you map the MAP weeks to deliverables we can sign off on (e.g., eval report, SOW, PO)?

If you can send the one-pager and the sensitivity table before EOD Tuesday, we can route to finance.

Kelsey Torrance

kelsey.t@cardiahealth.com | +1 212-555-0148

Subject: Re: MAP: unit-econ check & eval timeline — CardiaHealth

Kelsey — thanks, can do. Attaching two artifacts for procurement and the MAP:
- redwood-token-econ-onepager.pdf (one-page table + short notes)
- cardia-map-unit-econ.xlsx (sensitivity table with caching/batching scenarios)

Short answers inline:
1) One-pager: includes tokens/$ under three batching scenarios (none/moderate/aggressive) and 3 cache-hit assumptions (0/20/50%). We call out nominal per-request cost at 250 tokens and 1,200 tokens to show conversational vs. single-turn sensitivity.
2) Caching: prefix caching removes generation cost on repeated exact prompt prefixes — for clinician macros that hit frequently, even a 20% prefix hit reduces average per-request cost by ~15–25% depending on response length. KV caching (structured responses) reduces token generation by returning stored outputs for identical context keys and benefits higher-variance conversational flows. For MAP acceptance: we recommend measuring both during eval and using the 20% hit scenario as a conservative gating baseline.
3) The 7-day sample is perfect — we'll use that to populate the spreadsheet and run the eval prompt sample. Please include anonymized tokens-per-request distribution if possible.
4) Timeline mapped to deliverables (we'll include this in the MAP doc):
   - Week 0 (discovery): sample CSV + SLOs from Cardia — sign-off = traffic delivered
   - Week 1 (eval): Redwood runs 3 sequence-length perf & tokens runs; deliverable = eval report + token-econ workbook
   - Week 2 (reconcile): review results, agree pilot SOW scope & forecast; deliverable = SOW draft for PO
   - Week 3 (pilot start): pilot onboarding and dashboard access; deliverable = PO signed + pilot kickoff

We'll circulate the two attachments and the MAP doc by EOD Tuesday. Any special procurement contacts besides you and Marco we should include?

Thanks,
Olga
